medium_value.description: Make the wildcard matcher use one canonical implementation on every Node version, or specify a native fast path whose result is proven equivalent. Replace the native-result OR fallback expression and test fixtures where native and fallback matching disagree.
Move live housekeeping verification into an explicit post-merge gate with an owner and deadline, or identify it as deferred evidence and keep the affected bead open until that evidence exists.

Define the accepted evidence for the CPU-time migration separately from functional red-first tests, and specify how the quadratic stand-in is executed, measured, and recorded without entering production code.
Replace the open-ended known-host-local-red exception with a named allowlist of checks, expected failure signatures, and required evidence that each failure is unrelated to this change.

Add protected-path precedence tests combining an exact exclusion and a wildcard exclusion for the same file in both pattern orders. Assert that explicitly excluded files are absent from protectedKept.
Specify escaping for file paths and exclusion patterns rendered in PR summaries, and add fixtures containing Markdown delimiters and newlines.

Add explicit aggregate-budget acceptance tests for fetched contents: multiple eligible files, fetch-count exhaustion, synthesized diff overhead, and competition with existing patches. Specify that fetched files remain subject to the final file and byte budgets.
Specify that content requests use the immutable PR head SHA associated with the file listing, and add a test asserting the exact ref passed to getFileContent.

Define bounded handling for the base64 JSON fallback, including encoded-response overhead, decoded-byte limits, and malformed responses. Add adapter tests for a near-limit file returned as both raw text and base64 JSON.

Add a synthetic-patch fixture matrix covering empty content, missing final newline, CRLF, multibyte UTF-8, and content beginning with diff markers. Define line counts, newline markers, and byte accounting for each case.

Inventory all GitProvider implementations and typed test doubles before adding getFileContent, assign their required updates, and extend B's path allowlist where necessary. Define FileContentResult and its ownership in the contract commit.

Resolve the shared SKILL.md ownership by having A and B submit documentation snippets for the lead to integrate, or by defining a sequential documentation landing step with explicit conflict handling.

Add a content-fetch deadline and timeout test, and specify how the adapter terminates and cleans up a timed-out gh process. Document any inherited timeout if the existing adapter already provides one.

Make Q-3 a compatibility gate: enumerate discovered classifier consumers, assign updates for consumers that reject housekeeping, and require tests or explicit evidence that each consumer handles the new value.
Define a concrete non-degraded Bridgebuilder shipping gate and the outcome when two rounds or the USD 8 stop threshold are reached without an acceptable verdict.

Specify that matchesExcludePattern selects exactly one engine per call (native && path.matchesGlob available → path.matchesGlob, otherwise dotSegmentGlobMatch) and never ORs the two results; state the production default of opts.native (recommend false so production is one matcher on every Node version and the native engine is only the test oracle); state what { native: true } does on a Node without path.matchesGlob (silent fallback vs throw) so CI matrix behaviour is defined.

Have the lead run the single Q-1 read-only gh api probe during Task 1.0 (before worktrees are cut) and record the observed response shape(s) in the contract commit's report so B codes against a known shape; reconcile Dependencies ('one call') with the second live getFileContent probe in Task 1.E2E.

Add to Task 1.7 a lead-run integration check after landing A and B: a YAML config with a '**/*.yml' exclusion → truncateFiles → paged-fetch coverage record → rendered 'Protected paths kept (1)' line; mark Task 1.4's landing dependency on Task 1.2 in the Dependencies list.

Add a grep step to Task 1.1 for importers of simplifiedGlobMatch and callers of matchesExcludePattern outside A's allowlist (including progressive-truncation.test.ts, owned by B) with the rule that A reports required edits for the lead; alternatively move Task 1.5 to A so one implementer owns that test file.

State how fix-round patches are based: the lead fast-forwards the implementer's worktree to the landed head before each round, fix-round patches are exempt from red-first (or not), and rounds are capped (e.g. ≤ 2 per implementer) with escalation to the operator.

Define the decision when the Bridgebuilder stops under USD 8 remaining or still degrades after 2 rounds: hold the merge and escalate, or merge with a DEC row recording the missing verdict; amend G-5's 'non-degraded verdict' accordingly.
List the accepted host-local red test names (the KF-034 set) in the plan or in the reviewer.md template so a new red cannot be absorbed by the exception.
Assign distinct SKILL.md sections by heading to A (exclusion / protected paths) and B (coverage), and note that the lead resolves SKILL.md hunk conflicts when applying B's patch after A's landing.
Define the load condition for the three green runs (e.g. two concurrent npm test runs in the other worktrees, or a stated core-saturation method) and require it in the report.
Name the module that renders the PR summary section and add it to B's allowlist if it is not paged-fetch.ts.
Add a test or assertion that exclusion patterns (.reviewignore) are read from the reviewer's base checkout, not the PR head, or document the current source in SKILL.md.

Define isWildcardPattern's character set (*, ?, [, {) and state whether a non-wildcard segment pattern such as 'ci.yml' or 'workflows/' (which under Task 1.1 matches at any depth) may remove a protected file, or whether only a full-path-equal pattern may. Specify which pattern is recorded in protectedKept[].pattern when several user patterns match (first in order vs all). Enumerate DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATHS in the plan or cite the exact SDD C-2 list so A's fixtures, SKILL.md and B's rendering test agree.
Add FR-6 explicitly to the first acceptance bullet (or point to bullet 3 as FR-6's criterion), and state whether A returns one combined red/fix pair for Tasks 1.1 + 1.2 or two pairs.

State which Bridgebuilder build reviews the cycle-135 PR (the branch's regenerated dist or main's) and, if the branch's, record the PR summary's 'Protected paths kept' section and coverage protected_kept as live G-3 evidence.
State whether 'the operator confirms the proposed rows at the close' gates the merge (Task 1.9), the archive, or is post-ship.

Extend Task 1.0 to cover the whole cross-implementer contract: where FileContentResult is declared (types.ts vs ports/git-provider.ts); the options field through which protectedPatterns reaches truncateFiles (e.g. TruncationOptions.protectedPatterns); and a named owner for the caller-side plumbing of config.protectedPaths into the truncateFiles call(s) (B if the call lives in paged-fetch.ts, else A). Decide whether getFileContent is optional on the GitProvider port or grep every implementer/test double of the port and assign their updates.

Move 'the live confirmation on the next housekeeping merge' out of the sprint-close gate into a tracked follow-up with explicit non-blocking status in e2e.md (child bead or bd-nr5i6 left open), or produce it within the sprint: check whether the Task 1.9 archive PR's subject classifies as housekeeping under rule 1a and, if so, use its merge as the live confirmation and record the workflow run URL.

State how FR-5 satisfies 'red first': either exempt test-infrastructure changes with a rationale recorded in reviewer.md, or define the red artefact (the report-only quadratic stand-in with its failing output captured alongside the SHA of the measurement change).

Either relabel Task 1.2 (default protected list, replace-vs-merge config semantics) and Task 1.6 (Q-3 disposition) as kind: judgment, or add to each mechanical task 'report judgment points without deciding; the lead decides and writes the DEC row'.

Replace the truncation.ts line references :1292, :1442, :1515 and :666 with enclosing function names or a distinctive code anchor (the call expression) for each application site and the Loa-tier site.

Define the Q-3 outcome rule: any consumer of pr_type / PM_PR_TYPE that would fail or misroute on 'housekeeping' is a blocker returned to the lead before C's fix patch, not merely reported. Either add the notify-job assertion that the Risks section claims ('the workflow guards and notify pinned') to Task 1.6's test list, or drop the claim.

Add actionlint (or at minimum a YAML parse) of .github/workflows/post-merge.yml to C's tests and to the second acceptance bullet alongside bash -n, and name the rollback for a broken post-merge run on main (revert commit of the workflow hunk, who executes it).

Size maxBuffer for the base64-JSON fallback (≈ ceil(maxBytes × 4/3) + JSON envelope) or disable the fallback when the raw bound is exceeded; map ENOBUFS to too_large distinctly from other provider errors; state the per-call timeout for the gh api subprocess.

blockers.concern: Fetched files are described as pre-retained for pass 2, but the plan does not specify how their synthesized patches consume the shared byte, token, and file-selection budgets.
blockers.why_matters: Individually bounded downloads can collectively overflow the review budget, displace important files, or produce coverage records claiming review of content that never reached the model.
blockers.recommendation: Charge synthesized patches to the same aggregate budgets as ordinary patches before retention. Test mixed native and synthesized patches at each limit and verify coverage against the actual model payload.

blockers.concern: The content-fetch adapter decodes a base64 JSON envelope as a fallback when the raw media type is requested. The response body is PR-author-controlled file content, so an added file whose text is itself a GitHub-contents-shaped JSON object ({"content": "<base64 of benign text>", "encoding": "base64", ...}) would be decoded and the reviewer would review the decoded benign text instead of the real file. This is a new hiding path of exactly the class FR-1 is closing.
blockers.why_matters: A patch-less added file is the one place the attacker already controls both the eligibility (file size) and the bytes; a shape-sniffing fallback lets them substitute what gets reviewed, and the coverage record would show the file as reviewed with source contents.
blockers.location: Task 1.3 (B) — github-cli.ts getFileContent base64-JSON fallback; Risks & Mitigation 'raw media type returns base64 JSON'
blockers.recommendation: Do not sniff the body. Decide the decode path from the response headers (gh api --include, Content-Type: application/json vs raw) or settle on exactly one media type after the Q-1 probe and fail closed (no_patch) on any other shape. Add a fixture: a raw text file whose content is a fake envelope is reviewed verbatim. Make the lead own this judgment call rather than implementer B.

blockers.concern: The plan validates that ref looks like a commit SHA but does not require it to be the same immutable PR head used for the file listing and review.
blockers.why_matters: A PR update during collection could cause the synthesized patch to describe a different revision from the listed changes, making review and coverage evidence inaccurate.
blockers.recommendation: Capture the PR head SHA once, bind listing and content retrieval to it, record it in coverage evidence, and test a head change during collection.

blockers.concern: The wildcard matcher uses `(native && path.matchesGlob) || dotSegmentGlobMatch`. A native-only positive match therefore changes exclusion behavior across Node versions, contradicting the requirement for one matcher everywhere.
blockers.why_matters: A file can be excluded from review on one runtime and reviewed on another. The fallback cannot correct a native false positive.
blockers.recommendation: Use the custom matcher as the sole authority, or define and enforce equivalent semantics before enabling native matching. Test native-enabled and disabled results across the complete supported pattern grammar and supported Node versions.
